title: Build pipeline baseline
summary: What every build pipeline does before code can be merged and released: build, test, scan, and produce a traceable release image.
scope: Every repository that builds an application, a library or a container image. Documentation-only repositories are out of scope.

resources.title: Skill: check a pipeline against the baseline
resources.description: Reads your workflow files and lists what is missing.

requirements.title: Every pull request is built and tested
requirements.statement: Every pull request runs the build and the unit tests, and cannot be merged while they fail.
requirements.rationale: A main branch that does not build blocks everyone and hides real failures.
guidance: Use the shared build workflow for your language.
Make build and test required status checks on the main branch.

verification.description: A nightly check of the branch protection of every repository.

lookFor: A workflow change that removes the test step or marks it continue-on-error
Tests skipped with a condition that is always true

requirements.title: No critical vulnerabilities in a release build
requirements.statement: The dependency scan runs on every build, and a release build fails when a dependency has a known critical vulnerability with a fix available.
requirements.rationale: Most attacks on applications use known holes in libraries that were never updated.
guidance: Keep the dependency scan step of the shared workflow.
Update the dependency; if no fix exists, ask Cyber Security for an exception.

verification.description: Dependency scan in the build pipeline.

requirements.title: No secrets in pipeline files
requirements.statement: Workflow files contain no secret values; the pipeline reads secrets from Secret Manager through workload identity.
requirements.rationale: Workflow files are readable by everyone with access to the repository, and so are their logs.
guidance: Use the identity step of the shared workflow.
Never echo a secret in a run step.

verification.description: Secret scanner on every pull request.

lookFor: A token, key or password written in a workflow file
echo or set -x in a step that uses a secret

requirements.title: Pass the SonarQube quality gate
requirements.statement: New code passes the company SonarQube quality gate: no new bugs or security hotspots, and at least 70% test coverage of new lines.
requirements.rationale: The gate stops quality from sliding a little with every change.
guidance: Keep the sonarqube step of the shared workflow.
Mark false positives in SonarQube with a reason instead of lowering the gate.

verification.description: SonarQube status check on the pull request.

requirements.title: Use the Maven or Gradle wrapper
requirements.statement: Java builds run through the wrapper committed to the repository, so the build tool version is the same everywhere.
requirements.rationale: Different build tool versions give different results on laptops and in the pipeline.
guidance: Commit mvnw or gradlew with its wrapper properties.
Call ./mvnw or ./gradlew in the workflow, not mvn or gradle.

lookFor: A workflow step that calls mvn or gradle directly

requirements.title: Commit the lock file
requirements.statement: The dependency lock file is committed and the pipeline installs exactly what it lists.
requirements.rationale: Without it two builds of the same commit can contain different libraries.
guidance: JavaScript: commit package-lock.json and use npm ci.
Python: commit the lock file of your tool and install with --require-hashes.

lookFor: package-lock.json, poetry.lock or requirements lock deleted or added to .gitignore
npm install used in a workflow instead of npm ci

requirements.title: Cache dependencies between runs
requirements.statement: Pipelines may cache downloaded dependencies to make builds faster, keyed on the lock file.
requirements.rationale: Faster builds mean faster feedback on pull requests.

lookFor: A cache key that does not include the lock file
